prompts.baseline: Solve the user's problem by constructing one arithmetic expression. A separate calculator will evaluate your expression; do not manually evaluate it. Use the original given values, any conditioning information, and the requested units. Use standard unit-conversion constants when needed. Return ONLY one valid JSON object in this structure: {"explanation":"Briefly explain the setup.","expression":"Unevaluated arithmetic expression"}. Both fields must be strings. Keep explanation to at most 60 words. The expression may contain only plain integer or decimal numbers, parentheses, and +, -, *, /, including unary signs. Do not use names, functions, powers, LaTeX, Markdown, or text outside the JSON object.
prompts.syntax_clear: Solve the user's problem by constructing one arithmetic expression. A separate calculator will evaluate your expression; do not manually evaluate it. Use the original given values, any conditioning information, and the requested units. Use standard unit-conversion constants when needed. Return ONLY one valid JSON object in this structure: {"explanation":"Briefly explain the setup.","expression":"Unevaluated arithmetic expression"}. Both fields must be strings. Keep explanation to at most 60 words. The expression may contain only plain integer or decimal numbers, parentheses, and +, -, *, /, including unary signs. Do not use names, functions, powers, LaTeX, Markdown, or text outside the JSON object. Expression-format contract: expression must be one NUMERIC expression, not an equation or an intermediate symbolic rearrangement. For algebra, finish isolating the requested unknown in your setup, then put only a numeric right-hand-side expression for its value in expression. Never put variable names or an equals sign in expression. Use only ASCII digits 0-9, decimal points, spaces, parentheses, and the operators +, -, *, /. Write ASCII '*' for EVERY multiplication and '/' for division. Do not use Unicode operators, implicit multiplication, scientific notation, functions, units, or prose in expression. These are syntax examples only, unrelated to your question. VALID: '(2+3)*4'; '2*(3+4)'; '(7-1)/(5+2)'. INVALID: 'x = (2+3)*4'; '3*y+5'; '2×3'; '2∗3'; '2(3+4)'. Before sending, check that expression has balanced parentheses, no letters or '=', and an explicit ASCII operator between multiplied quantities. Return the original two-field JSON object; do not manually evaluate the expression.

analysis_plan.primary_population: 8 fresh development questions; 8 inspected regression questions reported separately
secondary_outcomes: joint method-valid numeric correctness as selected secondary diagnostic
limitations: Prompt clarification bundles numeric-only instructions, generic examples, and a pre-send syntax check; their individual effects are not separated.
Algebra-isolation reminder may affect formulation as well as syntax, so numerical changes are not purely calculator effects.
Two fresh items per family and one seed are descriptive development evidence.
Executable expressions can encode wrong reasoning; numerical tolerance does not certify formulation.
Joint method-valid numerical accuracy conditions on an intervention-dependent selected subset.
analysis_plan.no_adaptation: Freeze both prompts, tasks, seeds, and call order before inference; no prompt retuning, repairs, or retries.
